title: The Gavit Sisters Child-Kidnapping Murders
evidence: Police investigation established a pattern of repeated child kidnappings
Children were allegedly used to facilitate theft and other crimes
The investigation connected the sisters to multiple child deaths
The sisters were convicted of multiple murders and kidnapping offenses
The Supreme Court upheld their convictions and death sentences
modus_operandi: The sisters kidnapped children from public places and allegedly used them to facilitate theft and other criminal activities. Children who became difficult to control or were considered a liability were subsequently murdered, according to the prosecution case.
personality_disorder: No confirmed personality-disorder diagnosis should be assigned without a documented forensic psychiatric assessment. The documented behavioral pattern involved manipulation, exploitation of children, calculated violence, and repeated criminal behavior.
summary: Sisters Renuka Shinde and Seema Gavit were convicted for kidnapping and murdering children in Maharashtra during the 1990s. Their case is notable for the systematic exploitation of children as instruments for criminal activity and the subsequent murders of children who became liabilities.
